name: Food hall
summary: Multi-vendor food halls are usually adaptive reuse of an existing building; cost is driven by kitchen MEP density (hoods, grease, gas, power per stall), how fully the landlord builds out stalls, and the condition of the host building. Evidence spans TI-only operator budgets (~$15–175/SF, low confidence) to full public-market conversions ($367–$536/SF in 2014–15 dollars). Mid is a reasoned midpoint; no recent cost-consultant food hall benchmark was found.

typicalSize.method: e4: 'generally occupies between 10,000 and 25,000 square feet'; e1 28,000 SF; e2 30,000 SF hall. Mid 20,000 SF.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per acre of site: urban infill/ground-floor halls have high FAR; stand-alone suburban halls with surface parking ~0.2–0.35 FAR (≈ 9,000–15,000 SF/acre). Derived.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per SF: restaurant-type parking ~8–12 per 1,000 SF where required; urban halls often rely on shared/structured parking (Boston Public Market lists 325 spaces for 28,000 SF ≈ 0.0116/SF). Derived.

perPrimaryUnit.method: 2024 dollars, mixing evidence years: e3 RSMeans 2019 new restaurant $205/SF (≈ $260 in 2024); e2 Krog Street 2014 ≤ $367/SF of hall (≈ $530 in 2024, but spread over a larger building so lower in practice); e1 Boston 2015 $536/SF (≈ $750 in 2024, high-cost metro, may include soft). e4 TI-only budgets are far lower ($15–175/SF) because the shell and building systems already exist. Mid $375/SF = full conversion of an existing shell with landlord-built stalls, shared seating, bar and BOH; low $175 = second-generation restaurant/market space; high $650 = high-cost metro or ground-up with full stall fit-out. Escalation ratios are rough (~1.3x 2014/15→2024 and 2019→2024) and only used to position the mid; the build script handles formal escalation.

scope.notes: Conversion of an existing shell including MEP upgrades, common areas, central bar, BOH and landlord stall build-outs; minimal on-site work. For ground-up add a shell (see restaurant/retail types). Excludes land, soft costs, vendor kitchen equipment, seating FF&E.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (175/375 ≈ 0.47, rounded up); luxury ≈ high/mid (650/375 ≈ 1.73); premium interpolated.

systemSplit.method: Derived for an adaptive-reuse food hall: MEP-heavy (22 plumbing/grease ≈ 12%, 23 HVAC + kitchen exhaust/makeup air ≈ 15%, 26 electrical ≈ 12%) because each stall needs hood, grease and power; 09 finishes for a design-led dining hall; 02 selective demolition; 11 includes shared/landlord kitchen equipment and hoods. Ratios based on typical restaurant fit-out profiles; not sourced from a published food-hall estimate.

lineItems.name: Landlord-built vendor stall (hood, grease, utilities, counters)

cost.method: e4: fully equipped stalls 'can add $30,000 to $80,000 per stall'. Mid = midpoint. Qty ≈ 1 stall per 1,250 SF of hall (16 stalls in 20,000 SF).

lineItems.name: Shared kitchen exhaust / makeup air / HVAC systems

cost.method: e4 range 'Shared HVAC and commercial hood systems $50,000 – $200,000'; mid = midpoint. Likely low for 20,000+ SF halls.

lineItems.name: Central bar build-out (millwork, draft system, back bar)

cost.method: Derived allowance for a 40–80 LF center bar with draft system and coolers.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Common-area seating, tables, POS/tech: e4 lists dining furniture $20k–$80k and POS $10k–$30k for 10–25k SF (≈ $2–11/SF); designed halls with lounge seating run higher. Vendor kitchen equipment excluded. Derived.

pctOfHard.method: A&E for kitchen-heavy interiors (food-service consultant, MEP) plus permits, health dept review, leasing/curation. e4 lists A&E $15k–$50k for TI-scope projects. Derived from typical restaurant/retail soft-cost ranges.

softCosts.notes: Add tenant allowances / vendor incentives and pre-opening marketing separately; these are operating/leasing costs.

design.method: Adaptive reuse with uncertain existing conditions.

hard.method: Existing-building conversions commonly carry 10%+ construction contingency; e4-type operator guides advise 15–20% overall.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low hard × 1.15 soft rounded down (second-generation space) to Boston-type full fit-out with soft (e1 escalated ≈ $750) plus margin.

evidence.quote: The estimated construction cost of $15 million was funded with $6 million in grants ... Other dimensions 28,000 square feet retail space
evidence.scopeNotes: Indoor public market/food hall fitted into the ground floor of an existing state building; opened 2015. ≈ $536/SF of retail space. Likely includes vendor stall build-outs and some soft costs.

evidence.quote: The conversion of the 99 Krog Street building to Krog Street Market cost $11 million ... centered on a 30,000-square-foot ... food hall with various vendor stalls, five full-service restaurants and three larger traditional retail spaces.
evidence.scopeNotes: Adaptive-reuse conversion of a warehouse; cost covers the whole building (food hall + restaurants + retail), so ≤ ~$367/SF if only the 30,000 SF hall is counted; actual building area is larger. Opened 2014.

source.title: Restaurant - Commercial Construction Costs Per Square Foot (RSMeans model page)

evidence.quote: Restaurant with Brick Veneer / Wood Frame ... SubTotal 100% $164.13 ... Contractor Fees (General Conditions,Overhead,Profit) 25% $41.03
evidence.scopeNotes: 2019 RSMeans national model, 5,000 SF, 1 story, union labor. value = subtotal + 25% contractor fees = $205.16/SF; open shop = $186.33/SF. Building only: excludes the architectural fees (6–8%) shown on the page, sitework, FF&E. New-build single restaurant; lower bound for kitchen-heavy space.

source.title: How to Start a Food Hall Business

evidence.quote: Construction and vendor stall build-outs $250,000 – $1,500,000 ... Shared HVAC and commercial hood systems $50,000 – $200,000 ... Grease trap installation $10,000 – $50,000
evidence.scopeNotes: Operator startup budget for a leased 10,000–25,000 SF space (page: 'A food hall generally occupies between 10,000 and 25,000 square feet'); tenant-improvement scope only, ≈ $15–$175/SF. Undated blog, dollars assumed current. Also: fully equipped stalls 'can add $30,000 to $80,000 per stall'.

openQuestions: Find recent (2022+) food hall development budgets with SF (developer press, TIF/city incentive packets).
Separate ground-up vs. adaptive-reuse food halls; the type may need a shell add-on when ground-up.
